subject: Model fit evals: tool-calling & structured-output follow-up
messages:

Subject: Model fit evals: tool-calling & structured-output follow-up

Hi Samir —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and the recommended next steps to validate model fit for the summary+tool-calling workflow you demoed: 

1) Recommended models & variants
- Start with redwood-llama-13b-fx (fp16) for rapid iteration — good tradeoff on latency and accuracy.
- For higher quality on structured output, test redwood-pegasus-13b-int8 and our tuned redwood-instruct-7b as a low-cost fallback.
- We recommend running all three in parallel for a short A/B eval to quantify false-positive tool calls and schema violations.

2) Benchmarks & prompt sets (attached)
- Attached: benchmark_results_v1.pdf (initial latency/accuracy vs your sample traffic) and prompt_set_v2.jsonl (30 representative prompts).
- Drive folder with full harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Cbenchmark

3) Structured-output & function-calling checks
- Primary failure modes we saw: malformed JSON, missing required keys, and inconsistent types.
- We suggest: schema-first evals (JSON Schema validation), token-level regression checks (Jensen-Shannon on distributions), and end-to-end tool invocation tests with retry/backoff behavior.

4) Next steps / mutual action plan
- I will drop the eval harness + README into the Drive (see link above) and grant your SRE access. (attachments include eval_harness_instructions.md)
- Rishi to share a suggested schema-validator and retry strategy (e.g., max 2 retries with exponential backoff, idempotency keys).
- Schedule 30-min technical deep-dive next week to walk through the harness and initial run results.

Can you confirm the dataset we should use for the A/B run (full prod sample vs a 10k subset)? Also let us know who from infra will join the deep-dive.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: benchmark_results_v1.pdf (report, 14 pages); prompt_set_v2.jsonl (30 prompts); eval_harness_instructions.md

Subject: Re: Model fit evals: tool-calling & structured-output follow-up

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we kick off the evals: 

- JSON schema enforcement: do you recommend inline schema validation on the client (our side) before calling tools, or server-side post-processing to reject/repair outputs? If we do client-side, we worry about silent acceptance.

- Retries & idempotency: our platform has strict idempotency keys for downstream tool calls. If the model returns ambiguous tool payloads, would you recommend attempting a single automated repair (e.g., run through a canonicalizer) before a retry, or just surface to our orchestration layer?

We’ll start with a 10k subset from prod (sanitized) to keep cost/time reasonable. SRE (Aman Verma) will join the tech deep-dive.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform, Avery Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@averyanalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit evals: tool-calling & structured-output follow-up

Hi Samir — quick answers from the infra/ML side: 

- Where to validate: we recommend server-side canonical validation as the primary guard (Redwood runtime can perform JSON Schema validation as an intermediate step and emit structured error codes). Client-side validation is optional and useful for UX-level checks but should not be the only safety net.

- Repair vs retry: our playbook is: 1) attempt a single deterministic repair (e.g., close missing brackets, coerce numeric strings) using a lightweight canonicalizer; 2) if repair succeeds and passes schema checks, proceed; 3) otherwise trigger a single retry to the same model variant (not the fallback) with a clarified prompt that includes the schema example. If still failing, fall back to higher-quality variant (pegasus-13b-int8) or escalate to human review depending on criticality.

- Metrics / regression monitoring: capture schema-violation rate, tool-call false-positive rate, and structured-field-accuracy. We’ll hook those to Redwood Console so alerts fire if deviation > 2x baseline.

I’ll add a short example of the repair transform to the Drive and link it in the harness README. Also tagging a HubSpot note: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-2027-489

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Lead ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
